articles.title: Acid Carbon Mesh
articles.summary: Bright lime-green carbon weave with fine diagonal mesh lines, semi-matte with light sparkle. Reads as a vivid lime-yellow and green mesh with black gaps, bright on the right and darker green on the left; a fine dotted screen rather than carbon.
articles.what: Real-source pattern plate cropped to 2048 with paired image-derived dynamic spec channels. Up close: A tight grid of round dots, about 8 px, in acid yellow-lime and olive green on black, like a perforated mesh or halftone screen. The rows fan out from a pinch point just right of centre, so the dot lines radiate like a spiderweb or fan, and tone changes from bright yellow to deep green across it. From a distance: Reads as a vivid lime-yellow and green mesh with black gaps, bright on the right and darker green on the left; a fine dotted screen rather than carbon. Measured spec (average): metal 192, roughness 132, coat 160. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, truck / off-road.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Acid Carbon Mesh" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood: the fan centre reads as a focal point
Single placed fan: on side panels you only see part of the radiating lines
Dots fight numbers; use a solid white or black plate with a heavy outline.
Almost nothing: it is already a dense graphic
Pairs well with: black, matte grey, white, carbon dark.
pitfalls: Not a carbon weave: the render is a round dot grid, no woven strands
Not a diagonal mesh of lines: it is dots with a radial fan layout
Avoid: small numbers over fine weave, next to other green finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 192 (true metallic), roughness 132 (semi-matte), clearcoat 160 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over fine weave, next to other green finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: it is already a dense graphic; very soft large shapes at low strength
Patterns to avoid: dot, hex, weave or carbon patterns: moire with the dot grid; glitter patterns: lost in the dots

Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.summary: Dark indigo and magenta oil-slick swirl with a fine dotted mesh, iridescent holographic sheen over the whole panel. A glowing dotted mesh in a purple-to-magenta gradient with neon rim light; the dots blur into a shimmering grid and the colour ripple stays.
articles.what: Real-source pattern plate cropped to 2048 with paired image-derived dynamic spec channels. Up close: A fine hex-lattice circuit board: thin light traces joining glowing dots about 12-16 px apart, wandering in hexagon spirals, on a dark indigo field. A big soft warped ripple makes colour bands, teal-navy at the top running to hot coral-magenta at the bottom, with bright yellow-white flare at the. From a distance: A glowing dotted mesh in a purple-to-magenta gradient with neon rim light; the dots blur into a shimmering grid and the colour ripple stays. Measured spec (average): metal 108, roughness 70, coat 168. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, hood.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Holographic Oil Circuit" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood and roof: the round ripple composition reads on a large flat area
Side panels show the colour gradient fade
Dots are small enough that big thick white numbers still read; thin or dark numbers get lost.
Almost nothing: it is a single artwork plate, extra patterns hide the circuit
Pairs well with: gloss black, chrome, deep purple, silver.
pitfalls: Not a plain oil-slick: the dot-and-line circuit grid dominates
Not a random noise texture: it has a fixed round ripple composition
Avoid: busy numbers on top, flat matte neighbours.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 108 (pearl-level metal), roughness 70 (satin gloss), clearcoat 168 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: busy numbers on top, flat matte neighbours.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: it is a single artwork plate, extra patterns hide the circuit; a solid plate or black number panel is the only safe overlay
Patterns to avoid: other grids or hex patterns: moire with the lattice; camo: mud against the fine dots
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat: lifts the dots; none otherwise, spec is image-derived
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
